name: Claude's picks
rules: Copies my AI picks list: up to 10 stocks, at most 3 per sector, ranked by relative strength among liquid S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 stocks (the IBD formula: 40% weight on the last 3 months, 20% each on 6, 9 and 12).
Trades at about 10:00 New York time: sells stocks that left the list the night before and buys the new ones, about a tenth of the account each. Empty spots stay in cash.

Your overbought rule, as the paper accounts use it (from Oct 15): nothing is bought while the market's breadth or the stock's sector's is over the 75 line (the share of its stocks with the 10 EMA over the 20, last night); a pick skipped for that is bought later while it's still on the list. RSI and CCI no longer block a buy (you dropped that part of the rule on Oct 14).

A stock stays while it ranks in the top 20, unless your 4-hour exit sells it first (from Oct 14): a 4-hour bar closing with the 10 EMA under the 20 and the price under the 50 EMA, both at once, on the Trend view's 4H bars (9:30 AM-1:30 PM and 1:30-4:00 PM New York), checked every 30 minutes. A stock sold that way isn't bought back while it stays on the list. No other stop (in my 2014-2026 test, also selling below the 50-day EMA cut the return from 17.4% to 9.1% a year; your 4-hour exit wasn't part of that test).

Shares or options, whichever fits (your call, Oct 14): each pick gets about a tenth of the account. It buys a call by your rules (15-30 days out, delta 0.50-0.80, open interest over 500, a tight bid/ask), the one nearest 0.65 delta that fits that tenth, else the highest delta down to 0.15 that fits; if no call fits, shares. A call also sells at -50% (then it isn't bought back while the pick stays on the list) or 5 days before expiry (then it buys again in its place). My note: the edge in my test came from holding leaders for weeks, which 15-30 day calls lose to time decay.
In the test (S&P 500 as it was each day, 2014-2026) this made +19.4% a year against +14.5% for the average stock, with long stretches behind and a worst drop of -31%. The edge is not proven.
fills: Paper trades, no real money. Shares fill at Yahoo's latest 1-minute price, 0.05% worse, and fractional shares are allowed. Calls fill at the ask to buy and the bid to sell, plus $0.65 per contract each way. Yahoo's option quotes can lag by up to 15 minutes. Dividends are ignored.
